newsitem.title: USA: CME Jan lumber ends limit up on firmer cash ideas.
newsitem.headline: CME Jan lumber ends limit up on firmer cash ideas.

text.p: CME January lumber futures closed up their $10 limit, with others higher to sharply higher, on demand sparked by expectations for fimrer cash lumber markets next week, traders said.
January finished limit up at $392.20 per tbf, with March up $8.20 at $378.70. The rest rose $4.90 to $2.50.
Expectations are the cash market is bottoming and will start to show a firmer tone as early as next week. Seasonally, cash prices show strength late in the year, traders said.
"A lot of mills take down time late in the year" for the holidays, one trader said.

Cash prices had recently tumbled from record highs posted earlier in the month. Posting of individual mill export quotas caused uncertainty in the market and a sharp rally in cash prices, but actual demand for wood declined due to the high prices and easing in the housing market, they said.

Futures were also technically strong after breaking through a down-trend line early. Commission house Saul Stone was a leading buyer before selling at midsession. Prices rose the limit again late on mixed demand ahead of the early noon CST close due to Thursday's U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday.
